title: Datadog CEO Olivier Pomel on AI Security, Trust, and the Future of Observability
description:
Why is AI observability essential in modern applications? It holds the key to understanding app performance, user interactions, and system behavior in real-time, transforming passive monitoring into active insight. With the rise of complex AI systems, ensuring data accuracy and machine-led decisions becomes crucial.

Olivier Pomel, CEO of Datadog, offers a compelling perspective on the evolution of observability with AI. Under his leadership, Datadog has become a pivotal force in shaping the observability landscape. Olivier shares how Datadog's suite of AI-driven tools, including Watchdog and Toto, are redefining the future of automation and enhancing application management for thousands of companies.

What we cover:
• The evolution and significance of observability in modern applications
• Challenges AI presents to security and how trust is built
• How AI can transform automation within observability contexts
• What are the key opportunities for AI in observability?
• Exploring Datadog's AI product suite: Watchdog, Bits AI, and more

Chapters:
0:00 – Episode highlight: Cloud vs. AI fears
1:00 – Intro to Olivier Pomel and Datadog’s role in observability
4:00 – Three layers of AI opportunity: infra, apps on models, AI-powered automation
7:00 – Datadog’s AI product suite: Watchdog, Bits AI, LLM observability, Toto
10:00 – Trust and accuracy: Why false positives kill AI adoption
16:00 – Human-AI interaction models: Chat, copilots, agents, and UIs
18:00 – Automation in observability: When AI can safely take action
21:00 – AI security concerns: Prompt injection, untrusted code, and sandboxing
26:00 – The importance of building trust while embracing early risks
30:00 – Building Toto: A foundation model for time series
36:00 – Observability and the future of software development
42:00 – Observability in GenAI apps: From infrastructure to outcomes
47:00 – Expanding into product analytics and primary data
51:00 – The future UI of observability: Human-like agents and interfaces
53:00 – The danger of overhyping AI in observability
56:00 – Building an AI research team and the shock of AI’s rapid progress
